Sign up for free here to receive this newsletter in your inbox every Saturday. You’ll also get our weekly newsletter with an exclusive introduction from our senior editors. “Neurodivergent” was added to the Oxford English Dictionary in 2019, the ultimate acknowledgment that the many-types-of-minds paradigm was not just a fleeting hashtag. Used for people with conditions such as ADHD, autism and dyslexia, it reflects how many see themselves: simply different, rather than disordered. The scientific understanding of ADHD has been shifting in this direction, too. Neuroscientists have found that the formal diagnostic criteria for these conditions are ill-fitting, which explains why it is common for children to have more than one diagnosis. Schools in England are testing a new way to support neurodivergent pupils: focusing on their personal strengths, weaknesses and interests to help them thrive in the classroom—no diagnosis required. Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** A group of stock analysts used Claude to design proteins that could lead to antivenom. OpenAI bought a startup that helps drugmakers move faster the same day. ChatGPT now lets you lock chats behind a PIN. And OpenAI says one of its agents removed a safety monitor, then lied about it.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Claude:** Why did a stock research firm ask Claude to fight scorpions?

* **OpenAI:** What does OpenAI want with a drug development startup?

* **ChatGPT:** What chats are you hiding?

* **Shocking:** What did OpenAI's agent say when asked about the missing monitor?


----------







----------
## Claude took its first shot at an antivenom

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c6c7fabe-7774-4e1c-8ed9-6336b61e4689/dcbad177-4202-4567-a883-21cd923e3231.jpg?t=1792573803)
Caption: 

Scorpions sting more than 1.2 million people a year. The antivenom comes from horses injected with scorpion venom, and it can take months to make.

Anthropic [had Claude design an alternative from scratch](https://www.anthropic.com/research/claude-scorpion-toxin-binder-design). In 64 hours, it drew up 318,484 designs for tiny proteins that grab scorpion toxins before they hit your nerves.

Labs tested 211, and 17 stuck to the toxin they were built for. The best two grab a Mexican scorpion's toxin in about the same spot as an antibody known to protect mice.

* It started with Citrini Research, an investment research firm whose team mostly had no science background.

* Claude emailed the lab with its own questions, then kept designing once the answer came back.

* Citrini spent $49,997 on computing, $3 under budget, plus about $150,000 on lab tests.

* Anthropic says it isn't an antivenom yet, because nobody has tested the proteins in cells or animals.

One analyst got too excited and volunteered to get stung and test it himself. The plan is mice first.

81188.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/fintechpulse1141

Hey Everyone,
Good morning & happy Wednesday! Today, we’re diving into Anthropic’s new IPO prospectus that shows two straight profitable quarters, and yet the valuation talk just dropped from $2T to $1.5T (why slowing growth, not the $80.7B loss, is what cut the price, why the compute bill keeps climbing toward $750B even as Anthropic’s own cloud partners refuse it more capacity, why a weak debut would make the whole AI buildout more expensive to fund, & what’s next + bonus deep dives into How to Make Claude Limitless [ https://substack.com/redirect/27868185-a355-4ce7-86aa-e5aad7ce4357?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and The Top 10 Stocks Positioned to Benefit Most from Anthropic IPO [ https://substack.com/redirect/8155391f-af91-458e-bb0f-ada216119fc0?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside), and breaking down how a power cut at a single Google Cloud data centre in London took down Revolut’s app and cards across the UK, Europe and even the US (why one failed building took out a whole cloud region, what Monzo’s backup bank does differently, why regulators can’t fine Google but can come after Revolut, & what’s worth watching next + bonus dives into why Revolut is building its own Meta Muse & Grok Bot [ https://substack.com/redirect/2a8adffe-7ce8-4528-b849-38103835a957?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and a deep dive into Revolut [ https://substack.com/redirect/70ce57b2-9a3b-49f6-ad7e-72b267244da8?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside). So let’s jump straight into the important stuff 🌶️
Anthropic’s new IPO prospectus shows why profits didn’t save its $2 trillion valuation 😳📈
Following the money 💸 AI giant Anthropic has just posted two straight quarters of adjusted operating profit. Last month we said that result would make a $2 trillion IPO valuation  [ https://substack.com/redirect/4c127e81-82af-4462-868b-24651d7bbc89?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]defensible [ https://substack.com/redirect/4c127e81-82af-4462-868b-24651d7bbc89?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], yet some investors are now discussing about $1.5 trillion… 👀
On October 20, the Wall Street Journal obtained a newer draft of Anthropic’s S-1 prospectus. It shows an $80.7 billion first-half net loss, compute commitments above $600 billion that could reach $750 billion, and cloud partners that have started refusing Anthropic extra capacity. Let that sink in… 😳
Let’s dive deeper into this and unpack what cut $500 billion from the valuation talk, and how much of that loss is real. We also cover what two stumbling AI listings this month mean for Anthropic’s November roadshow, and the December revenue number the valuation now depends on...

Nová pozícia, viac zodpovednosti a atraktívnejší titul na vizitke. Zamestnanec, ktorý sa po rokoch práce dočká povýšenia, by mal mať dôvod na spokojnosť. Lenže nie vždy sa kariérny postup prejaví aj na výplatnej páske. Niektoré firmy ponúkajú ľuďom vyššie pozície bez toho, aby im zároveň zvýšili mzdu. V zahraničí sa pre tento jav udomácnilo označenie dry promotion, teda povýšenie bez finančného prilepšenia. Nejde o úplnú novinku, ale v čase, keď firmy dôslednejšie kontrolujú náklady, môže byť takýto postup spôsobom, ako obsadiť dôležité pozície bez navýšenia mzdového rozpočtu. Z odborníka sa stane manažér, výplata zostane rovnaká Typickým príkladom môže byť skúsený špecialista, ktorý po odchode svojho nadriadeného prevezme vedenie tímu. K pôvodným úlohám mu pribudne organizovanie práce kolegov, kontrola výsledkov či zodpovednosť za dodržiavanie termínov. Firma mu zmení názov pozície, no zvýšenie mzdy odloží s vysvetlením, že naň momentálne nemá rozpočet. Zamestnanec sa tak ocitne v situácii, keď musí okamžite zvládať náročnejšiu prácu, zatiaľ čo lepšie finančné podmienky zostávajú iba prísľubom. Takáto ponuka nemusí byť automaticky nevýhodná. Pre človeka, ktorý sa chce dostať k vedúcej pozícii, môžu byť nové skúsenosti cenné aj pri ďalšom hľadaní práce. Problém nastáva, ak zamestnávateľ nedokáže povedať, kedy a za akých podmienok sa zmení aj odmeňovanie. Rozdiel je tiež v tom, či zamestnanec získava skutočné rozhodovacie právomoci alebo mu firma iba presúva ďalšiu agendu. Vyššia pracovná pozícia totiž automaticky neznamená aj to, že človek má väčší vplyv na fungovanie tímu.  Úspora, ktorá sa firme nemusí vyplatiť Povýšiť vlastného zamestnanca býva pre spoločnosť jednoduchšie než hľadať nového manažéra na trhu. Interný kandidát pozná kolegov, procesy aj firemnú kultúru a spravidla nepotrebuje taký dlhý čas na zaškolenie. Ak však s novou funkciou nepríde primerané ohodnotenie, pôvodne pozitívna správa sa môže postupne zmeniť na zdroj nespokojnosti. Najmä, ak sú podobné pozície v iných spoločnostiach platené lepšie. Pre firmu to môže mať nepríjemný dôsledok – človek, ktorého si chcela povýšením udržať, získa manažérsku prax a následne ju využije pri uchádzaní sa o lepšie platené miesto u konkurencie.
